subject: reasoning
question:
How many triangles are there in the given figure ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd8bc1ac1a6cb93320654c9e83b4510c59754f084bcb1c28be541fb66d03f79a.png]
solution:
The number of triangles in the given figure is shown below:

1) Number of triangles = [Number of parts × (1 + Number of parts)] ÷ 2 = Total triangles

= [2 × (1 + 2)] ÷ 2

= [2 × 3] ÷ 2

= 6 ÷ 2

= 3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/883d3de3beb0afe0eb5db5d0b1e4442c899e58678f6cc6a0fcee67734882830b.png] 

2) Number of triangles = (Number of parts × Number of diagonals)

= 4 × 2 ⇒ 8 

Here, as there are two same parts, therefore '8 + 8' = 16 triangles

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93c5fa8f4d98d0eeacfa11a3c4160d8bdd975fc36bf538aa51ee20af2597c825.png] 

3) Number of triangles as marked = 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68abc17519bbd24fcdfe3ef629996b60a879b77bc81f396f260cbad4d2d5a90a.png] 

Thus, total number of triangles are 3 + 16 + 4 = 23

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.
